html:
Kannauj was the city on the Ganges that became the prize capital of north India after the Guptas. On the 600 and 700 maps, the name stands for the kingdom ruled from it.

The Maukharis made it their capital in the 6th century. Then Harsha ruled from Kannauj from 606 to 647 over most of the north. The Chinese monk Xuanzang visited his court and described a great religious gathering there. Harsha's push south was stopped on the Narmada by Pulakeshin II. In the 8th century King Yashovarman ruled here, before Lalitaditya of Kashmir defeated him.

Because whoever held Kannauj could claim to rule the north, three powers fought over it for a century: the Gurjara Pratiharas, the Palas and the Rashtrakutas. This was the Tripartite Struggle. The Pratiharas won it and held the city from 816. The city's older name, Kanyakubja, goes back to Panchala.
sum: Kannauj was the city on the Ganges that became the prize capital of north India after the Guptas. On the 600 and 700 maps, the name stands for the kingdom ruled from it.
